notes.text: The buggy snippet's result is nondeterministic and is not machine-checked (only fixedSource is run). On a sandbox container limited to one CPU, lost increments are much rarer and the buggy code might print 4000000; the prompt therefore says 'usually'. The fact-checker may want to confirm the race reproduces in the sandbox.

Assumed the JIT does not keep the captured field `counter` (a field of the closure class) in a register across the inner loop or fold the loop into a single addition; either would change how often the race shows, though not the defect itself.
Assumed Interlocked.Increment with 4 threads x 1,000,000 contended increments completes well within the 10 second sandbox deadline (expected well under a second).
Assumed the managed-threading-best-practices page still contains the recommendation to use Interlocked.Increment instead of a lock for simple increments; not re-fetched.
meta.dotnetVersion omitted because the behaviour does not depend on the .NET version.
